question: After removing the benchmark directional confound, what genuine policy competence and complementarity remain?
requalifies: Stage 3F.6-P (first stage of the Stage 3F.6-P.1D MINIMAL_REQUALIFICATION_SEQUENCE)

roles.CAL: selection (strongest regime, best single policy, cascade order)

partitions.sealing: HOLDOUT and OOD policy evidence is generated only after this plan and the open-phase report are committed
partitions.holdoutSupportedSlice: HOLDOUT is also reported restricted to curriculum levels present in DEV or CAL, because DEV/CAL contain levels 0-1 only while HOLDOUT contains 0-2
partitions.priorExposure: the Stage 3F.6-P.1D frozen integrity diagnostics published P(zero-cost optimal) and P(RESOURCE correct | zero-cost optimal) on HOLDOUT and OOD, which implies RESOURCE accuracy there; no other sealed policy quantity was computed before this plan

evidence.source: every stored corpus row is rebuilt from its combination with the frozen symmetric generator; the policy surface is the symmetric legal surface in canonical-frame order, exactly as Stage 3F.6-P.1D presented it
evidence.fidelity: world hash, distinct action keys and every deployable/control choice must equal the stored corpus row (tolerance 0)
captured: D4 twin choices on the corpus equivariance sample (combination index divisible by 25; 5 transforms)
evidence.greedy: GREEDY is read from the corpus (it requires the simulator); it is a reference, not requalified

metrics.accuracy: chosen action is in the horizon-optimal set (regret 0); over proposing episodes; Wilson 95% interval
metrics.coverage: proposing episodes / partition episodes; abstention = 1 - coverage, with abstain reasons
metrics.regret: raw regret: mean, median, p90, p95, max (nearest-rank); mean has a bootstrap 95% interval
metrics.normalizedRegret: regret / max regret over the legal surface of that episode (0 when every action is optimal); scale-free, comparable across partitions
metrics.catastrophic: raw regret >= 100 (Stage 3F.6 contract catastrophicRegret); raw-scale caveat applies
metrics.confidence: mean confidence; accuracy by fixed bins [0,0.2),[0.2,0.4),[0.4,0.6),[0.6,0.8),[0.8,1]; ECE over those bins; AUROC of confidence for correctness. RESOURCE confidence is declared cost spread, not a probability; ECE is descriptive only; constant-confidence policies report NOT_APPLICABLE
metrics.aboveChance: accuracy minus UNIFORM_LEGAL_EXPECTATION on the same proposing episodes; paired bootstrap 95% interval
metrics.strongestRegime: on CAL, the binary regime (either side) with the highest policy accuracy among regimes with at least 200 proposing CAL episodes; that regime is then reported on HOLDOUT and OOD

bootstrap.generator: mulberry32 seeded by sha256("STAGE3F6P1E_BOOTSTRAP:" + partition + ":" + slice)

binary.ZERO_COST_AVAILABLE: some legal action has declared cost 0
binary.ZERO_COST_OPTIMAL: some optimal action has declared cost 0 (oracle-derived; slice only, never a decision input)

categorical: surfaceQuartile (DEV quartiles of legal action count)
regimes.matrixValues: accuracy of the policy inside the regime (proposing episodes), its share of the regime where it is uniquely best, and n; every value is computed, none assigned

nuisanceFactors.ABSOLUTE_DIRECTION: accuracy by chosen MOVE direction (4 levels); the chosen-direction share is reported as a behavioural preference, not a shortcut
nuisanceFactors.ACTION_ID_ORDER: accuracy of the policy vs ID_PERMUTED_MEAN and vs ID_REVERSED on the same episodes (paired)
nuisanceFactors.D4_TWIN: on the equivariance sample: choice equivariance rate and accuracy on transformed twins vs the original episodes (paired)
nuisanceFactors.SEED_FAMILY: NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: exactly one seed was used per partition, so seed family is confounded with partition; reported as the partition comparison

shortcutAudit.nuisanceFlag: a categorical factor flags when (max - min) accuracy over levels with >= 100 proposing episodes exceeds max(0.08, 3 * SE of that difference); a paired factor (ID order, D4 twin) flags when |difference| exceeds max(0.03, 3 * paired SE). NUISANCE_DEPENDENCE requires the flag on BOTH CAL and HOLDOUT.
shortcutAudit.taskFlag: same numeric rule; replicated flags are reported as REGIME_DEPENDENT (expected for task structure, never by itself a shortcut)
shortcutAudit.artifactRule: COST_PRIOR_EXPLAINS when the HOLDOUT paired 95% upper bound of (accuracy - artifact baseline accuracy) is < 0.05; REASONING_BEYOND_COST_PRIOR when its lower bound is > 0

complementarity.primarySet: HISTORICAL_ROUTED (the Stage 3F.6-T frozen routed set, so the result is comparable to Stage 3F.6-P)
complementarity.best: proposing members at the minimum regret (ties kept); uniquely best = sole member of that set
perPolicy: regret avoided vs always-RESOURCE (per episode, uniquely-best episodes)
regret introduced when mis-selected (mean excess over the best member, episodes where the policy proposes but is not best)
regime lift of uniquely-best episodes (P(regime | uniquely best) / P(regime))
complementarity.oracleFallback: an episode where no member proposes uses the RANDOM_LEGAL_V1 control action
complementarity.bestSingle: on CAL: the deployable policy with coverage >= 0.99 and minimum mean regret (ties: higher accuracy)
deterministicBaselines: FIXED_PRIORITY_CASCADE: abstaining specialists (OBJECTIVE, THREAT, NEXUS V1, NEXUS V2) whose CAL accuracy-when-proposing exceeds the best single, tried in descending CAL accuracy, then the best single; untrained, not a router, not a candidate
complementarity.headroom: THEORETICAL_ROUTING_HEADROOM = PERFECT_SELECTOR(set) minus best single (accuracy, mean regret, mean normalized regret), paired bootstrap 95% intervals, HOLDOUT primary, OOD robustness
complementarity.materialHeadroom: ROUTING_HEADROOM_MATERIAL when the HOLDOUT accuracy headroom lower bound >= 0.05 for the primary set

classification.appliedOn: HOLDOUT; CAL shown alongside; OOD annotates
rules: SHORTCUT_DEPENDENT if any NUISANCE_DEPENDENCE flag, or the declared artifact baseline explains the accuracy (COST_PRIOR_EXPLAINS)
REDUNDANT if, in its marginal set, marginal oracle accuracy gain < 0.005 and marginal mean normalized-regret reduction < 0.005
KEEP if ABOVE_CHANCE (paired lower bound > 0) and accuracy when best-available >= 0.75 and marginal accuracy gain >= 0.02
REDESIGN_CANDIDATE if marginal accuracy gain >= 0.02 and accuracy when best-available < 0.50
annotations: OOD_DEGRADES if OOD accuracy - HOLDOUT accuracy <= -0.10, else OOD_HOLDS
classification.resourceQuestion: RESOURCE is GENUINE_RESOURCE_REASONING only if REASONING_BEYOND_COST_PRIOR; ZERO_COST_PRIOR_ONLY if COST_PRIOR_EXPLAINS; otherwise MIXED; any replicated nuisance flag adds ANOTHER_ARTIFACT
classification.nexusQuestion: NEXUS status is re-derived from these rules; the Stage 3F.6-P REDESIGN_CANDIDATE is not carried forward
classification.historical: a Stage 3F.6-P conclusion SURVIVES when the new class equals the historical class; accuracy comparisons with Forge V1 are descriptive only (different worlds, different regret scale)

acceptance.PASS: every integrity check holds; a negative policy result is a valid PASS
FAIL: evaluation leakage (sealed evidence generated before the plan freeze commit)
non-reproducibility (evidence fidelity < 1 or certification not byte-identical on --check)
post-HOLDOUT tuning (plan or policy source changed after the freeze commit)

readiness.SYMMETRY_CERTIFIED: P.1C and P.1D certificates intact and the corpus equivariance flags all 1.0
readiness.CORPUS_LINEAGE_CLEAN: content hash bound and zero overlap/duplicate/leakage
readiness.POLICY_RESULTS_REPRODUCIBLE: evidence fidelity 1.0 and deterministic evidence replay
readiness.AFFECTED_POLICIES_REQUALIFIED: every deployable policy has a class
readiness.EXPERT_DIVERSITY_READY: stage PASS and the competence matrix is computed (the separate expert-diversity audit may begin)
readiness.ROUTER_VALUE_AUDIT_READY: stage PASS and headroom is computed (the separate Router-value audit may begin)
readiness.READY_FOR_STAGE3G: false by construction in this stage

definitions.RESOURCE_PRESERVING_V1: frozen Stage 3F.6-A producer: minimum declared cost, ties by action identity
definitions.NEXUS_SELECTOR_V1: frozen Stage 3C nexusRelationalSelector; the routed NEXUS_SELECTOR of Stage 3F.6-T/3F.6-P
definitions.NEXUS_SELECTOR_V2_CANDIDATE: Stage 3F.6-P.1 candidate (PROTECT gate on V1); candidate-only, never promoted
definitions.OBJECTIVE_TARGETING_V1: frozen Stage 3F.6-A producer; abstains unless a legal action targets an observed critical entity
definitions.THREAT_COVERING_V1: frozen Stage 3F.6-A producer; abstains unless a legal action covers an observed unsupported threat
definitions.CHEAPEST_CLASS_UNIFORM: exact expectation of a uniform choice among the minimum-declared-cost legal actions (distinct keys); decision-time computable; the matched artifact baseline for RESOURCE (the cost prior with no tie information)
definitions.ID_REVERSED(<deployable>): the unmodified policy re-run with action identities relabelled so their lexicographic order is reversed; the choice is mapped back to the true action. Isolates the identity tie-break.
definitions.ID_PERMUTED_MEAN(<deployable>): mean over 8 seeded random identity relabellings of the unmodified policy (tie-randomised policy)
definitions.GREEDY: non-deployable reference: best immediate transition value, canonical-frame tie-break (uses the simulator)
definitions.PERFECT_SELECTOR(<set>): non-deployable diagnostic ceiling: per episode, the proposing member with minimum regret
definitions.RANDOM_LEGAL_V1: frozen deterministic control seeded by the observed world digest
definitions.UNIFORM_LEGAL_EXPECTATION: exact expectation of a uniform legal choice (distinct keys)

notEvaluated.reason: Stage 3F.6-A non-deployable simulator-search reference; not stored in the symmetric corpus and requires the simulator at decision time

policySet.prime: no Prime or synthesis baseline consumes these policies in the symmetric lineage; nothing to requalify
